drivingQuestion: How is the mishna to be read so that it does not contradict the baraita permitting even a single chapter or verse?
outcomeNote: This unit is the answer to the ורמינהו of the preceding unit; on its own it opens with no question of its own.

segments.he: הָכִי נָמֵי קָאָמַר: אִם יְכוֹלִין לְהַתְחִיל וְלִגְמוֹר אֲפִילּוּ פֶּרֶק אֶחָד אוֹ אֲפִילּוּ פָּסוּק אֶחָד עַד שֶׁלֹּא יַגִּיעוּ לַשּׁוּרָה — יַתְחִילוּ, וְאִם לָאו — לֹא יַתְחִילוּ.
segments.en: The Gemara responds: «That is also what» the tanna of the mishna «said» and this is the conclusion drawn from his statement: «If one can begin and conclude even one chapter or one verse before they arrive at the row» of consolers, «they should begin. And if not, they should not begin.»

moves.summary: the mishna is re-read as saying just what the baraita says, so the contradiction raised in the previous unit dissolves
moves.about: the contradiction between mishna and baraita over whether a single chapter or verse suffices dissolves once the mishna is read as saying the same thing

what the mishna means: begin if even one chapter or verse can be completed before reaching the row, and otherwise do not begin
